A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Optimal Rates for Feasible Payoff Set Estimation in Games. Their main text, equations, Figure 1, Table 1, and complete Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs, and illustrative payoff-set geometry. Neither the main text nor Appendices A-D report original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical analysis and illustrative geometry without adding empirical outcomes. Table 1 remains a symbols table, and the appendices contain proofs and auxiliary lemmas.

M1.justification: Procedure 1 still collects action samples, estimates the players' strategies by empirical frequencies, and returns the corresponding feasible payoff set. Its steps, inputs, outputs, and linear-feasibility representation are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluation tasks. Infinite-action games are newly mentioned only as future work, not as an evaluated setting.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against Procedure 1. The newly cited Poiani et al. (2026) work is discussed as inspiration for future research, not introduced as a baseline.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, evaluation metrics, splits, or training budgets are introduced or revised. Theorem 4.1's sample-complexity statement concerns a theoretical guarantee, not an experimental setting.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical supplementary analyses appear in either version. Figure 1's analytical examples and the appendix constructions and counterexamples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The appendix concentration arguments remain unchanged.

E6.justification: No measured outcomes or empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. Figure 1 retains the same illustrative parameter values and geometric findings.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 changes the support-learning numerator from log(1/delta) to log(n/delta). Its footnote also broadens the factors hidden by tilde-O from log(n) factors to logarithmic factors generally, qualifying the stated guarantee. The explicit sampling formula in Appendix B and all appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim of minimax-optimal feasible-payoff-set estimation for exact and approximate equilibria in general-sum and zero-sum games. The added future directions do not expand the claimed achieved contribution.

C2.justification: A new Section 3.1 footnote explains that targeting an approximate-equilibrium payoff set can relax the learning requirement even for exact-equilibrium demonstrations while retaining approximations of the true payoffs. The conclusion also adds infinite-action games as a future direction and elaborates on instance-dependent analysis.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, linear-constraint representation, and explicit sample prescription in Appendix B are retained. No implementation, hardware, code-access, or data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Poiani, Bernasconi, and Celli (2026), Pure exploration with infinite answers, and connects it to future instance-dependent analysis with infinitely many candidate answers. The existing related-work discussion otherwise remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short explanatory footnote and expands the conclusion, updates author affiliation and publication information, and places the Impact Statement after Acknowledgments. The main narrative and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1's left-panel tick labels are repositioned, while its geometry, values, and caption remain unchanged. Added text and front-matter changes cause limited layout reflow; Procedure 1 and Table 1 retain their display structure.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision by qualifying Theorem 4.1's hidden logarithmic factors consistently with the unchanged Appendix B sampling formula. The added explanation of relaxed payoff-set learning and expanded scope discussion also improve interpretability. These are limited gains; the central algorithm and proofs remain unchanged.
